walkthrough:
Combine the two fractions on the left-hand side over a common denominator:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{(1 + \cos\theta)^2 + \sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta(1 + \cos\theta)}$$

Expand the squared binomial and apply $\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1$ in the numerator:
$$\text{Numerator} = 1 + 2\cos\theta + \cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1 + 2\cos\theta + 1 = 2 + 2\cos\theta = 2(1 + \cos\theta)$$

Cancel the common factor $(1 + \cos\theta)$ with the denominator:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{2(1 + \cos\theta)}{\sin\theta(1 + \cos\theta)} = \frac{2}{\sin\theta} = \text{RHS}$$

Substitute the proven identity into the equation:
$$\frac{2}{\sin\theta} = \frac{3}{\cos\theta} \implies 2\cos\theta = 3\sin\theta \implies \tan\theta = \frac{2}{3}$$

Find all solutions for $\theta$ in the range $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$:
$$\theta_1 = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) \approx 33.69^\circ \approx 33.7^\circ$$
$$\theta_2 = 180^\circ + 33.69^\circ \approx 213.7^\circ$$
$$(\text{Solutions: } \theta = 33.7^\circ, \quad 213.7^\circ)$$
